table_assessment.assessment_notes: ICD decision-aid table containing descriptive device placement, outcome and adverse-event facts alongside medication continuation, counselling, device-removal and deactivation instructions. Sixteen non-decorative response cells are annotated; the two 'Does not apply' cells are non-assertive and omitted.

factual_relations.notes: The ICD may stop the dangerous rhythm.
The rhythm is stated as potentially causing sudden death.
Electrical shock is the stated ICD mechanism.

text_units.verbatim_text: An ICD may stop a dangerous heart rhythm that could cause sudden death by giving an electrical shock to the heart.

factual_relations.notes: Sudden death risk is conditional on a dangerous rhythm occurring.
Inference directly licensed by the explicit higher-risk-without-ICD comparison; human review should confirm predicate choice.

text_units.verbatim_text: Without an ICD, you will have a higher risk of dying suddenly if a dangerous heart rhythm happens.

entities.surface_form: ICD will need to be replaced

factual_relations.notes: The ICD is placed under the skin.
The leads are described as going into the heart.
Replacement timing is stated as about 5-10 years and battery-dependent.

normative_assertions.notes: This is future device-course information, not an instruction to the reader.

text_units.verbatim_text: An ICD is put under the skin on your chest and wires ("leads") go into your heart. You will probably stay one night in the hospital. In about 5-10 years, when the battery runs out, and the ICD will need to be replaced.

factual_relations.notes: The source explicitly says medicine treats the heart problem.

text_units.verbatim_text: You can continue to use medicine to treat your heart problem.

factual_relations.notes: ICD recipients are stated to be less likely to die suddenly from the rhythm.
The quantitative sentence states death over five years; it does not label that numeric outcome as sudden death. Corrected in independent second-pass source-fidelity adjudication.

header_path: Will I live longer with an ICD?

text_units.verbatim_text: Patients with an ICD are less likely to die suddenly of a dangerous heart rhythm. With an ICD, 29 out of 100 patients with heart failure will die over a 5-year period. This is 7 fewer deaths than if they did not have an ICD.

factual_relations.notes: Patients without ICD are more likely to die suddenly from the rhythm.
The quantitative sentence states death over five years; it does not label that numeric outcome as sudden death. Corrected in independent second-pass source-fidelity adjudication.

header_path: Will I live longer with an ICD?

text_units.verbatim_text: Patients without an ICD are more likely to die suddenly from a dangerous heart rhythm. Without an ICD, 36 out of 100 patients with heart failure will die over a 5-year period.

factual_relations.notes: Shock probability is reported as 20/100 over five years; 80/100 are reported not shocked.
Patients describe the shock sensation with the stated comparison.

header_path: Will I get shocked by the ICD? What will that feel like?

text_units.verbatim_text: Over 5 years, 20 out of every 100 patients who have an ICD will get a shock. 80 out of 100 patients will not get shocked. Patients say that getting shocked is like "being kicked in the chest."

factual_relations.notes: Negation is conditional on not receiving the ICD; the schema cannot directly encode absence of exposure.

header_path: Will I get shocked by the ICD? What will that feel like?

text_units.verbatim_text: You will not get a shock from an ICD if you don't get an ICD.

factual_relations.notes: Bleeding is reported for 4/100 patients.
A serious problem is reported for 2/100, with examples retained as adverse-event entities.
Infection is reported for 1/100 patients.
Infection may require ICD removal.

header_path: What are the risks of getting an ICD?

text_units.verbatim_text: 4 out of every 100 patients will have some bleeding. 2 out of every 100 patients will have a serious problem, such as damage to the lung, a heart attack, or a stroke. 1 out of every 100 patients will get an infection, which may require removing the ICD.

factual_relations.notes: The absence of placement is stated to avoid placement risks; the condition is carried by the decision-aid column.

header_path: What are the risks of getting an ICD?

text_units.verbatim_text: You will not have the risks of placing an ICD.

factual_relations.notes: The source explicitly negates symptom improvement.
The source explicitly says the ICD does not cure the heart problem.

header_path: Will an ICD improve my symptoms?

text_units.verbatim_text: Having an ICD will not improve your symptoms or cure your heart problem.

factual_relations.notes: The heart problem is stated to influence symptoms.

header_path: Will an ICD improve my symptoms?

text_units.verbatim_text: Your symptoms will be influenced by your heart problem.

header_path: Are there things I cannot do?

normative_assertions.notes: The reader is directed to discuss activity limitations with a doctor.

text_units.verbatim_text: This depends on your heart problem. Talk to your doctor about driving limitations and other activities.

header_path: Are there things I cannot do?

normative_assertions.notes: The counselling instruction applies even without ICD implantation.

text_units.verbatim_text: Even without an ICD, talk with your doctor about driving limitations and other activities.

header_path: Can the ICD be taken out?

normative_assertions.notes: Removal is discouraged except for infection or battery-depletion replacement timing.

text_units.verbatim_text: It is best not to remove the ICD unless it gets infected or it is time to have it replaced when the battery runs out.

factual_relations.notes: The source states deactivation can occur without surgery.

header_path: Can the ICD be turned off?

normative_assertions.notes: Turning the ICD off is mapped to DISCONTINUE and is recommended under the stated terminal-illness condition.

text_units.verbatim_text: Yes, the ICD can be turned off without surgery. This is recommended if a person is likely to die from another illness.
